title: Customer Research for Ad Creative: A Practical Guide
summary: Turn interviews, reviews, sales calls, and support conversations into sharper ad hooks, objections, proof, and creative briefs, without inventing insight.
body_markdown:
## Build an objection and angle map


Group repeated evidence into:


- Problem angles
- Outcome angles
- Mechanism angles
- Proof angles
- Objection angles
- Alternative/comparison angles


Prioritize patterns that are frequent, important, relevant to the product, supportable, and visually demonstrable.


## Turn research into a video brief


> For \[audience\] in \[situation\], show \[problem/desire\] and prove \[promise\] through \[mechanism/evidence\] using \[format\], then ask them to \[action\].


Choose UGC when the language and situation carry the idea, a demo when product behavior is the proof, and animation when the mechanism is difficult to see.


## What not to do


Do not invent quotes, extrapolate from one unusual review, expose personal information, treat support complaints as marketing permission, or use AI to produce “customer language” without a source. Verify every testimonial and result separately.
